subject: MAP: Traffic replay orchestration and capacity owners — proposed windows
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@greengrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Traffic replay orchestration and capacity owners — proposed windows

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I’m sharing a concise MAP milestone focused on the performance validation step (traffic replay + peak QPS run). Goal here is to align owners, surface dependencies, and propose 2 candidate test windows so your SREs can confirm availability.

Executive summary (one line): Redwood will run a traffic-replay performance pass using a representative 10k request sample to validate dedicated capacity sizing and latency SLAs; target close for the MAP remains 2027-05-20 pending successful replay and a short validation review.

Proposed milestone: Performance validation — traffic replay + peak QPS run
- Target date range: 2027-05-03 to 2027-05-07 (primary) or 2027-05-10 to 2027-05-14 (fallback)
- Duration: 4 hours of controlled replay + 2 hours of soak/analysis
- Owners: GreenGrid ops (network, firewall rules) -> Sara Liu; Redwood ops -> Marissa Cole (runbook lead) and Karthik Iyer (capacity tuning)
- Deliverables: runbook execution notes, latency/cost report, KV cache hit-rate, and a pass/fail decision for go/no-go on dedicated sizing
- Dependencies: secure sample payloads (traffic-sample-10k.jsonl), network egress rules to Redwood VPC, test API keys with limited scopes, and a pre-provisioned reserved pool (if desired)

Immediate asks for GreenGrid:
1) Confirm which of the two windows works for your SREs (and list a primary contact and pager)
2) Share a sanitized traffic sample (we attached a template: traffic-sample-10k.jsonl) or confirm Redwood can use the synthetic template
3) Approve temporary test keys + IP allowlist for 10.0.0.0/24 (we can adapt range)

Next steps from Redwood:
- I’ll update the MAP spreadsheet (attached) with owners and the confirmed window once you confirm.
- Marissa will follow up with a short pre-run checklist and the ops runbook.

If the windows above are too tight, suggest two alternatives and we’ll re-align. Thanks — aiming to keep this low-friction so we don’t block the May commercial close.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0178

Attachments: MAP-draft-GreenGrid-v2.xlsx (MAP milestone table), traffic-sample-10k.jsonl (sample), ops-runbook-template.pdf
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@greengrid.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@ggrids.io>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Traffic replay orchestration and capacity owners — proposed windows

Thanks Alex — appreciate the clear plan. Quick notes from our side:

- Primary contact: Tom Baxter (SRE lead) — tbaxter@ggrids.io, pager available during CI windows
- The primary window 2027-05-03 to 2027-05-07 looks tight for us (we have a release on the 4th). The fallback 2027-05-10 to 2027-05-14 is better.
- We will provide a sanitized traffic sample by 2027-04-28. We prefer Redwood use our sample rather than synthetic to exercise our true distribution.
- Network: we can open an allowlist for the test on 2027-05-09 (to give our netsec a day to validate). Exact CIDR to follow.

One ask from procurement: before we run a peak QPS replay, can Redwood confirm if the dedicated pool is required for the replay, or if a hosted burst option with capacity tags is sufficient for a validation pass? That affects our budget owner’s approval timeline.

Tom — can you confirm availability for 2027-05-10 (preferred) and whether you need a preliminary test on 2027-05-07 for a smoke run?

Thanks,
Sara
Director, Platform Engineering | GreenGrid Media
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@greengrid.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Traffic replay orchestration and capacity owners — proposed windows

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the quick replies and for raising the procurement question — good call. Short answers:
- For the validation replay we can run on hosted burst if GreenGrid prefers; the hosted burst plan will exercise our same runtime and give valid latency and correctness signals but may not reflect worst-case dedicated tail-latency under sustained load. If you want a strict dedicated-sizing recommendation, we’ll need a reserved pool for the replay (we can spin a short-term reserved pool for the test window).
- Cost/approval impact: short-term reserved pool for a 4-hour validation typically maps to one day of a small reserved instance and we’ll provide an estimated dollar figure in the runbook before the test.

Operational plan suggestion:
- 2027-05-07: 1-hr smoke run (hosted burst) — verifies credentials, allowlist, and sample parsing
- 2027-05-10: 4-hr traffic replay (target) — either hosted burst or reserved pool per your procurement OK

Karthik will take point on capacity sizing and the tuning knobs (quantization/ batching profiles) and Rishi will own post-run quality checks and regression flags. I’ll send the pre-run checklist and a short cost table by Monday.

Marissa Cole
Manager, Reliability Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@ggrids.io>

Tom Baxter
